# Code walkthrough

For every file: what it does, why it is built that way, and what happens with bad input. These are the three
questions Srinivasan may ask about any file (brief §12.2). Written by Claude to help Matt learn the code.

## Project settings

**`manage.py`**: runs Django's commands (`runserver`, `migrate`, `test`, and ours). Generated by Django.

**`config/settings.py`**: every setting. Values that differ between a laptop and the deployed site (secret
key, debug, database, allowed addresses, upload folder) come from environment variables, so secrets never
enter the repository. Bad input: with debug off and no secret key it refuses to start, rather than run
with a known key.

**`config/urls.py`**: sends `/admin/` to Django's admin, `/accounts/` to Django's login pages, and everything
else to `core/urls.py`.

**`config/wsgi.py`, `config/asgi.py`**: how a web server such as gunicorn starts the app. Generated by Django.

## Data

**`core/models.py`**: the database tables. `User` (with a role), `Provision` (a playbook entry),
`Agreement`, `Clause`, `Flag` (a finding), `FlagDecision` and `Disposition` (the record). Decisions and
outcomes are add-only, and `PROTECT` stops anyone deleting a flag that has decisions: that makes the record
trustworthy. Bad input: the database refuses a confidence outside 0–1 (a check constraint), and every
choice field accepts only its listed values.

**`core/migrations/`**: instructions that create and change the tables, generated from `models.py` by
`makemigrations`. Never edited by hand.

**`core/admin.py`**: shows the tables in Django's admin screens at `/admin/`, where the administrator
manages users and the playbook.

## Pages

**`core/urls.py`**: the list of addresses and the view for each.

**`core/views.py`**: one function per page. Each one checks who is asking before doing anything: login first
(`@login_required`), then role or ownership. Submitting only saves the file; reading happens elsewhere. Bad
input: an unknown agreement number gives "404 Not Found"; the wrong role or someone else's agreement gives
"403 Forbidden"; invalid form input redisplays the page with the error.

**`core/forms.py`**: the intake form (refuses the wrong file type, files over 20 MB, a non-PDF renamed to
.pdf, a needed-by date in the past), the findings form (refuses supporting words that are not in the chosen
clause), and the decision and outcome forms (a reason is required; conditions are required when clearing
with conditions; only allowed outcomes are offered).

**`core/permissions.py`**: who may see and do what. Staff roles see every agreement; requesters only their
own. Only reviewers and approvers review, only the approver finishes an escalated agreement, and nobody
reviews their own submission. Kept in one file so the rules are easy to check.

**`core/templates/`**: the HTML pages. `base.html` holds the header, menu and styling. Django escapes all
text, so contract text can never inject HTML into a page.

**`core/templatetags/review_extras.py`**: the `highlight` filter that marks the supporting words inside a
clause on the review page. It escapes the text before adding the mark.

## Reading and identification

**`core/reading.py`**: reads a document. `extract_text` gets the text from a PDF (pdfplumber) or a .txt
file; `split_into_clauses` splits it at section headings and cuts very long clauses at sentence ends;
`read_agreement` claims an agreement in one database step (so two workers never read the same file) and
saves the clauses. Bad input: a scanned PDF, a damaged PDF, a password-protected PDF or an unknown file type
marks the agreement "Could not read document" with a reason; any unexpected error is recorded the same way
instead of leaving the agreement stuck.

**`core/rules.py`**: text rules, one regular expression per CUAD category a pattern can find. The finding is
the whole sentence around the match. Measured by `evaluate_identification`.

**`core/auto_identify.py`**: after reading, runs the rules and saves their findings. If every playbook
provision has an automatic method, the agreement goes to review; otherwise it waits for a person on the
identification screen. Runs only once per agreement.

**`core/review.py`**: the review rules: recording a decision, which outcomes are allowed, recording the
outcome, and the agreement's history. Bad input: an outcome before every finding is decided, or one the
rules do not allow, raises `ReviewError`, which the page shows as a message. If two people record an
outcome at once, only the first succeeds.

## Evaluation

**`core/cuad.py`**: reads the CUAD dataset: category counts and descriptions, and each contract's text with
its labeled clauses.

**`core/evaluation.py`**: scores identification against CUAD's labels. A flag counts as correct when its
text overlaps a labeled clause for the same category. Also picks the check set.

## Commands (`core/management/commands/`)

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `seed_demo.py` | Demo logins, the playbook, sample agreements. Safe to repeat. |
| `load_playbook.py` | Loads `seed/playbook.csv`. Refuses an unknown severity. |
| `process_agreements.py` | The reading worker: reads waiting agreements and runs the rules. `--watch` keeps it running. |
| `try_reading.py` | Tries reading on a folder of contracts without saving; reports clause counts and timing. |
| `count_categories.py` | Counts CUAD's labeled clauses per category. |
| `evaluate_identification.py` | Scores the rules on the check set and writes a report. |
| `evaluate_modified.py` | Scores them on the modified standard agreements. |

## Tests

**`core/tests.py`, `core/test_review.py`, `core/test_auto.py`**: about 50 automated checks: intake and
permissions, reading and splitting (with a small PDF built inside the test), identification, review rules,
reports, highlighting, the rules, and the scoring. Run with `python manage.py test`.

## Deployment

**`start.sh`**: what the deployed site runs: database changes, static files, demo data, then the website and
the reading worker side by side. If either stops, the service stops so Railway restarts it.

**`Procfile`**, **`.python-version`**: tell Railway to run `start.sh` and which Python to use.

**`requirements.txt`**: the Python packages, with exact versions (`pip freeze`).

## Data files

**`seed/playbook.csv`**: the playbook. **`seed/check_set.txt`**: the check set. **`seed/sample_contracts/`**:
demo contracts from CUAD. **`seed/modified_agreements/`**: the modified standard agreements and their answer key.
